text: Git branching helps developers work on different tasks without affecting the main code. A common practice is to create a feature branch for each new feature or bug fix. This keeps the main branch stable while you experiment safely. When your work is ready, you merge the feature branch back into the main branch. Before merging, teams often open a pull request so others can review the changes and discuss them. This version control workflow makes collaboration easier and reduces mistakes. By using branches, merges, and pull requests together, teams can build software in an organized and reliable way.
